# RNBO codebox numeric and math smoke fixtures

These 43 original MIT-authored programs exercise exact, individually inventoried RNBO codebox spellings. They use `codebox~`, not GenExpr. Each standalone `.rnbo` file equals the embedded `rnbo_extra_attributes.code` in its five-box, two-input/two-output patch. Unary calls operate per lane; `pow`, `atan2` and `hypot` reverse their input order for the right output. No parameters or resources are authored.

`reference.py` defines independent mathematical expectations before hardware execution. Model IDs 300–311 cover exact simple/integer operations, including actual signed subnormals and common signed-32-bit-safe conversion boundaries. Round is explicitly nearest integer with ties away from zero; fract uses signed `x - trunc(x)`. Sign-zero and operation-output zero signs are diagnostics. NaN-related functions receive finite inputs only, so no nonfinite-replacement behavior is claimed. Codebox integer aliases are tested as numeric function calls; event-store or patcher behavior is not inferred.

Models 312–337 cover standard square/cube roots, exponentials, logarithms, power, trigonometric/hyperbolic functions and angle conversions. Each case has its own finite, valid input domain, with expected output magnitude below 8. The fixed absolute smoke error limit is `2e-6` against a once-binary32-rounded mathematical reference. Simple operations have limit zero. These limits are authored before device output; no post-output fitting or optimisation is performed. The catalog records them explicitly.

This batch uses zero automatic preparation warm blocks so domain-restricted functions are not first executed with an invalid all-zero input. Four manual and sixteen timed callbacks use the same valid input vector and stateless expectation. These are short functional checks, not complete input-domain, mode, alias or floating-environment qualification. No previous patcher, signal-object, codebox alias or GenExpr result transfers to another spelling.

Portable tests are in `tools/test_smoke_rnbo_codebox_numeric_reference.py`. Export/preparation and target module results are retained separately under ignored `build/research/rnbo-codebox-numeric-smoke-v1` and `build/hardware/rnbo-codebox-numeric-smoke-modules-v1`. Failures remain at their actual stage, without fallback source. Generated RNBO C++ stays private. A 4 KiB module arena is only the structural ceiling; actual memory and callback timing require hardware execution. Build wall time is not DSP performance.

The [XIAO hardware run](../../../../evidence/xiao-smoke-rnbo-codebox-numeric.json) completes all 43 programs: 40 pass and `round`, `isdenorm`, `fixdenorm` retain output mismatches. All memory/allocation gates pass. Fourteen callback costs are queued for later CPU review; no reference, limit or DSP implementation was changed after the run.
